01 · Introduction

Dear John and Emily,

Thank you for inviting us into the next chapter of your website and your communications.

We loved building the new website with you. Since 1967, the Clubs have grown from one clubhouse in Raleigh to ten locations across Wake and Johnston counties, with Ralph leading the organization for fifty of those years. The new site gives that history a home online, along with the young people, alumni, staff, and supporters who are part of it.

John's notes describe a full year ahead: a History page with a tribute to Ralph, a Stories page, printed newsletters and videos, media relations, and the Breakfast of Champions. We'd love to help you do all of it, at a pace that fits your team and your budget.

We would be excited to help you:

  • Keep the website current and secure
  • Send a monthly e-news and keep social media and press outreach on a regular schedule
  • Produce seasonal pieces two at a time, in the order you choose
  • Build Phase 2 of the website, including the History and Stories pages

As you know, Liminal works with equity-centered nonprofits, and we clarify what an organization says before we design how it looks. For you, that means your website and your e-news tell the same story about what happens at a Club.

We see this as a partnership. You'll set the priorities each month, and we'll do the work and keep you posted along the way.

We look forward to the conversation,

Bill Cummings

CEO, Liminal

07 · How we work together

Two projects at a time, in the order you choose

Your monthly work runs on a regular schedule: website edits, strategy and SEO, the e-news, social media content, and one press release a month.

Seasonal projects move through a shared queue. We'll keep two projects in production at a time, and when one finishes, the next one on your list starts. You set the order, and we'll look at the queue together on a monthly call so seasonal pieces are ready when you need them.

This keeps your full list in scope without raising the monthly fee. If something urgent comes up, you can move it to the front of the line.

Phase 2 of the website runs on its own track, outside the two-project limit, so new pages don't slow down your marketing.
